how: Starters propose the conversion and the later Jubjub build, then supply a build sequence that others can follow.
Calls recruit people first to make the Jubjub and later to keep the threatened figure alive.
Participants answer defence calls with brief declarations of help or a commitment lasting until sleep.
Participants propose an eight-bit pet and work out feature order and foot colours.
An outsider starts the community name and members refit its letters to accommodate neighbouring art.
A proposed build sequence is followed by a report that the figure is done.
Participants identify a Jubjub feature and share a Wocky workplan, supporting specific drawing instructions rather than a single settled official template.
Members watch the figure, declare themselves defending, and repeatedly fix altered eye pixels.
Explaining the blue lettering reveals friendly damage and elicits apologies and an explicit stop to removing it.
Reports distinguish observed recolouring and suspected lost figures from uncertain attribution and a denial of responsibility.
An objection to defacing art is accepted and followed by admissions, withdrawal, and offers to restore the mango.
A treaty request receives an offer of red pixels for retaining the Jubjub and a promise of non-harm.
Former opponents help with the new figure and receive an explicit promise of reciprocal help.
Members maintain other people's works and divide attention between the Jubjub and another restoration without reporting a bargain.
A visitor brings a treaty proposal into the build thread and receives a direct negotiating answer.
The first project calls for converting existing art and coordinates an ambush before the later repair.
Participants mark completion and thank the people who built together.
Survival is celebrated through collective pride, small personal contributions, and enjoyment of defending alongside other projects.
Retrospective accounts record the ending alongside lost lettering and an unrealized second pet.
A participant preserves a repaired moment in a screenshot and another directs readers to the figure in a timelapse.
Members use familiar game politics and avatars to joke about neighbours while disputing the half-communist comparison.
The element's canvas-worth component appears as members reassess the activity as fun, warlike, and artistic.
Reported bots change letter colours, but their operators and any adoption by this room remain unidentified.
A joint-defence proposal and retrospective protection of a neighbour do not establish an agreed coalition or its organization.
Bargaining to retain space establishes negotiation but leaves host jurisdiction and approval rules unresolved.
The documented withdrawal and shrinkage accommodate existing art rather than follow erasure of the room's mark.
Searching for free space and retrospectively reporting few hands do not establish a contemporaneous judgment that holding the spot was impossible.
Naming, an unfinished plan, and an individual's renewed interest do not show a collective decision to continue the temporary project.
Canvas jokes and a sarcastic redesign proposal do not establish that the host subreddit was staging an April Fools takeover.
A grievance about destruction during the canvas event supplies no evidence of a rivalry inherited from before it.
Task sequencing, colour discussion, and a reported consensus show local decisions but cannot test the model's population frequency or establish a command structure.
The target conversion and later political joke or canvas grievance do not identify a pre-existing tie naming an attack rival.
Attribute anti-Rainbow-Road blame and Void sympathy to the speaker recalling destroyed work rather than treating them as the room's collective alignment.
A reported consensus and an individual's divergent faction preference do not show a dispute over who can bind the room.
Lost lettering and a preferred screenshot are recorded without an observed dispute over cleaning or authoritatively rewriting the shared final record.
The build call is answered by a concrete sequence and later completion, supporting the local call-to-building path.
A starter's proposal can itself be the recruiting call, so the two acts need not form distinct successive stages.
The defence call explicitly recalls hours spent building and names ongoing erasure as the reason to keep the figure alive.
Defence prompts an approach to neighbours and proposals for shared protection and help in return for space.
The later treaty exchange ends with an explicit promise not to harm the Jubjub.
Treat border agreements as one route to restraint because ethical objections and restoration commitments also precede a peaceful-neighbour agreement.
Maintenance pressure and unidentified bots do not show that this room adopted automation because manual defence was insufficient.
Completion and the remembered shared build provide the named achievement for thanks and collective pride.
Celebration precedes screenshot and timelapse discussion, but the concepts do not establish that celebrating caused people to preserve the work.
Preservation and renewed individual interest do not establish a subsequent collective decision to carry the temporary effort elsewhere.
The documented moves protect neighbours, while low manpower is reported after survival rather than as the cause of relocation.
A shared workplan need not settle design because colour choices, additional pets, and misunderstood lettering remain open after instructions circulate.
The help appeal receives a short commitment to try until sleep, supporting the acceptance branch without establishing what every reader did.
Joining can be explicitly conditional on sparing another person's territory rather than a bare assent.
Help can follow repaired relations before a later defence crisis, so maintenance strain is not the only route to intergroup assistance.
Border negotiation produces an offer of pixel help for space and a non-harm promise, establishing a bargain but not verified delivery.
Keep promised exchanges distinct from performed help when the record contains conditional offers without proof of delivery.
Recruitment and an attack proposal can be the same initiating act rather than separate mobilization and later redirection.
The conversion call elicits a reasoned ethical objection, explicit agreement, and efforts to retreat and restore the targeted work.
A complaint about targeting leads into restoration and an explicit exchange proposing peaceful proximity.
An attack can close through repair and former opponents helping rather than sustain adversarial contest talk.
Common defence is proposed and neighbour protection later recalled, but the intervening agreement and coalition formation remain unseen.
Recruitment through a hoped-for sticky and Discord invitation does not establish a flood of posts causing host-subreddit boundary rules.
Treaty talk and reported consensus do not reveal a subsequent challenge to who may commit the room.
Effective defence requires distinguishing planned friendly changes from hostile erosion before removing pixels.
Pixel maintenance can be fitted between an existing game routine rather than replace ordinary participation.
Part of defence and lettering coordination runs through a live chat whose decisions are not reproduced in the public thread.
A participant may withdraw attention once timelapse visibility seems secure even while other people continue defending.
A cross-room help request permits divergent personal responses shaped by earlier canvas experiences rather than binding every member to the proposed side.
Sparing one neighbour can require resizing the signature while participants negotiate competing obligations to other nearby art.
Post-event celebration includes naming proposals and jokes without showing that participants settle a single name.
Celebrating a surviving figure can coexist with lost lettering and an unfinished second design.
Anticipated visibility in a timelapse can count as success before placement ends rather than only document an achievement after closure.
Leaving occupied art makes a later build acceptable to a helper whose participation is conditional on that withdrawal.
Repair is followed by former opponents helping the new figure and receiving an explicit reciprocal commitment.
People can receive protection instructions before understanding the event, so late explanation and location help remain necessary after mobilization.

statement: Returning canvas visibility to ordinary community participation
how: Expected publicity has a reported individual return and coincident chat arrivals, supporting a local feedback path without proving collective growth.

statement: Choosing maintenance standards beyond any single group's mark
how: Participants maintain several groups' works and disagree whether clean space improves the canvas or prevents renewal.
